						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

															RRB NTPC Recruitment 2024 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

															

															Exam Pattern

															**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 100
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 40 Questions
																	Mathematics: 30 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
																	Total Marks: 100
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 120
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																	Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 50 Questions
																	Mathematics: 35 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
																	Total Marks: 120
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

															
																Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
															

															**4. Document Verification:

															
																Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
															

															Syllabus

															**1. General Awareness:

															
																Current Affairs (National and International)
																Indian History and Culture
																Geography
																Indian Polity and Constitution
																Economy
																General Science
																Environmental Issues
															

															**2. Mathematics:

															
																Number Systems
																Algebra
																Geometry
																Trigonometry
																Mensuration
																Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
															

															**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

															
																Analogies
																Blood Relations
																Coding-Decoding
																Syllogism
																Direction Sense
																Decision Making
																Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
															

															**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

															
																Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
															

															Preparation Tips:

															
																Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
																Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
																Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
																Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

															RRB NTPC Recruitment 2024 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

															

															Exam Pattern

															**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 100
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 40 Questions
																	Mathematics: 30 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
																	Total Marks: 100
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 120
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																	Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 50 Questions
																	Mathematics: 35 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
																	Total Marks: 120
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

															
																Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
															

															**4. Document Verification:

															
																Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
															

															Syllabus

															**1. General Awareness:

															
																Current Affairs (National and International)
																Indian History and Culture
																Geography
																Indian Polity and Constitution
																Economy
																General Science
																Environmental Issues
															

															**2. Mathematics:

															
																Number Systems
																Algebra
																Geometry
																Trigonometry
																Mensuration
																Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
															

															**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

															
																Analogies
																Blood Relations
																Coding-Decoding
																Syllogism
																Direction Sense
																Decision Making
																Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
															

															**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

															
																Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
															

															Preparation Tips:

															
																Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
																Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
																Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
																Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

			RRB NTPC 10+2 Level Recruitment 2025 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

			Exam Pattern

			**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

			
				
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 100
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 40 Questions
					Mathematics: 30 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
					Total Marks: 100
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

			
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 120
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
					Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 50 Questions
					Mathematics: 35 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
					Total Marks: 120
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

			
				Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
			

			**4. Document Verification:

			
				Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
			

			Syllabus

			**1. General Awareness:

			
				Current Affairs (National and International)
				Indian History and Culture
				Geography
				Indian Polity and Constitution
				Economy
				General Science
				Environmental Issues
			

			**2. Mathematics:

			
				Number Systems
				Algebra
				Geometry
				Trigonometry
				Mensuration
				Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
			

			**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

			
				Analogies
				Blood Relations
				Coding-Decoding
				Syllogism
				Direction Sense
				Decision Making
				Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
			

			**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

			
				Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
			

			Preparation Tips:

			
				Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
				Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
				Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
				Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

			RRB NTPC 10+2 Level Recruitment 2025 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

			Exam Pattern

			**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

			
				
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 100
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 40 Questions
					Mathematics: 30 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
					Total Marks: 100
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

			
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 120
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
					Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 50 Questions
					Mathematics: 35 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
					Total Marks: 120
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

			
				Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
			

			**4. Document Verification:

			
				Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
			

			Syllabus

			**1. General Awareness:

			
				Current Affairs (National and International)
				Indian History and Culture
				Geography
				Indian Polity and Constitution
				Economy
				General Science
				Environmental Issues
			

			**2. Mathematics:

			
				Number Systems
				Algebra
				Geometry
				Trigonometry
				Mensuration
				Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
			

			**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

			
				Analogies
				Blood Relations
				Coding-Decoding
				Syllogism
				Direction Sense
				Decision Making
				Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
			

			**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

			
				Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
			

			Preparation Tips:

			
				Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
				Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
				Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
				Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

															RRB Section Controller CEN No. 03/2026: Exam Pattern/ Syllabus

															Computer Based Test (CBT)

															
																
																Total Duration: 120 minutes.
																
																
																Total Questions: 100 objective-type questions with multiple choices.
																
																
																Negative Marking: There will be negative marking, with a penalty of 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
																Normalization: The CBT will be held in multiple shifts, and a normalized score will be used for shortlisting candidates for the CBAT.
																
															

															CBT Syllabus

															The syllabus for the CBT is divided into three sections:

															
																
																Analytical and Mathematical Capability:

																
																	
																	Mathematics: Includes topics like Averages, Percentages, Profit, Loss & Discounts, Time, Speed, Distance, Power & Work, Algebra, Linear Equations, Arithmetic Progression, LCM, HCF, Geometry, Area & Volumes, Probability & Statistics (both basic level).
																	
																	
																	Data Analysis & Interpretation: Includes Multi-source Data Analysis, Examination, analysis and Inference drawing from text, tabular data and data represented graphically (charts, graphs, scatter plot, pie chart, statistical curve distribution, Venn Diagrams), Data Sufficiency, and Data Arrangement.
																	
																
																
																
																Logical Capability:

																
																	
																	Logical Reasoning: Includes Binary Logic, Syllogism, Clocks & Calendars, Assumptions, Blood Relations, Family Tree, and Solving logic-based puzzles.
																	
																	
																	Reading Comprehension: Passages would be given from subjects like History, Society, Literature, Science, Environment, Abstract, Mythology, Technology and Culture. Candidates will need to understand the main idea, supporting idea, application, logical structure, and style of the passage to answer questions.
																	
																
																
																
																Mental Reasoning:

																
																	
																	Analogy: Identifying the relationship between two terms and applying it to another pair.
																	
																	
																	Series Completion: Identifying the pattern in a sequence of numbers and predicting the next term.
																	
																	
																	Solving Coding-Decoding type questions, Solving Ranking and Arrangements based problems.
																	
																
																
															

															
															Section-Wise Question Distribution (Indicative)

															
																
																Analytical and Mathematical Capability: 60 questions
																
																
																Logical Capability: 20 questions
																
																
																Mental Reasoning: 20 questions
																
																
																Total: 100 questions
																
															
															

															Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

															
																
																Shortlisting: Candidates equal to 8 times the number of vacancies will be selected for the CBAT.
																
																
																Qualifying Marks: Candidates must secure a minimum T-Score of 42 in each of the test batteries to qualify. This applies to all candidates, regardless of community or category.
																
																
																Exam Type: This test contains questions and answer options only in English and Hindi.
																
																
																Negative Marking: There will be no negative marking in the CBAT.
																
																
																Merit List: The merit list will be drawn based on the candidates' performance in both the CBT (70% weightage) and the CBAT (30% weightage).
																
															

															Document Verification (DV)

															
																
																Candidates will be called for document verification based on the merit list prepared using a 70% weightage for marks obtained in CBT and a 30% weightage for marks obtained in CBAT.
																
																
																In case of a tie in marks, the merit position will be determined by age (the older person is placed higher) and then by the alphabetical order of the name.
																
															

															Minimum Qualifying Marks

															The minimum percentage of qualifying marks for the CBT is as follows:

															
																
																UR (Unreserved) & EWS (Economically Weaker Section): 40%
																
																
																OBC (Non-creamy layer): 30%
																
																
																SC (Scheduled Caste): 30%
																
																
																ST (Scheduled Tribe): 25%
																
															

															Note: The qualifying percentages for PwBD (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities) candidates are relaxed by 2 marks in case of a shortage of qualified candidates.

																Candidates will be called for document verification based on the merit list prepared using a 70% weightage for marks obtained in CBT and a 30% weightage for marks obtained in CBAT.
																
																
																In case of a tie in marks, the merit position will be determined by age (the older person is placed higher) and then by the alphabetical order of the name.

															Note: The qualifying percentages for PwBD (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities) candidates are relaxed by 2 marks in case of a shortage of qualified candidates.

															RRB Section Controller CEN No. 04/2025: Exam Pattern/ Syllabus

															Computer Based Test (CBT)

															
																
																Total Duration: 120 minutes.
																
																
																Total Questions: 100 objective-type questions with multiple choices.
																
																
																Negative Marking: There will be negative marking, with a penalty of 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
																Normalization: The CBT will be held in multiple shifts, and a normalized score will be used for shortlisting candidates for the CBAT.
																
															

															CBT Syllabus

															The syllabus for the CBT is divided into three sections:

															
																
																Analytical and Mathematical Capability:

																
																	
																	Mathematics: Includes topics like Averages, Percentages, Profit, Loss & Discounts, Time, Speed, Distance, Power & Work, Algebra, Linear Equations, Arithmetic Progression, LCM, HCF, Geometry, Area & Volumes, Probability & Statistics (both basic level).
																	
																	
																	Data Analysis & Interpretation: Includes Multi-source Data Analysis, Examination, analysis and Inference drawing from text, tabular data and data represented graphically (charts, graphs, scatter plot, pie chart, statistical curve distribution, Venn Diagrams), Data Sufficiency, and Data Arrangement.
																	
																
																
																
																Logical Capability:

																
																	
																	Logical Reasoning: Includes Binary Logic, Syllogism, Clocks & Calendars, Assumptions, Blood Relations, Family Tree, and Solving logic-based puzzles.
																	
																	
																	Reading Comprehension: Passages would be given from subjects like History, Society, Literature, Science, Environment, Abstract, Mythology, Technology and Culture. Candidates will need to understand the main idea, supporting idea, application, logical structure, and style of the passage to answer questions.
																	
																
																
																
																Mental Reasoning:

																
																	
																	Analogy: Identifying the relationship between two terms and applying it to another pair.
																	
																	
																	Series Completion: Identifying the pattern in a sequence of numbers and predicting the next term.
																	
																	
																	Solving Coding-Decoding type questions, Solving Ranking and Arrangements based problems.
																	
																
																
															

															
															Section-Wise Question Distribution (Indicative)

															
																
																Analytical and Mathematical Capability: 60 questions
																
																
																Logical Capability: 20 questions
																
																
																Mental Reasoning: 20 questions
																
																
																Total: 100 questions
																
															
															

															Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

															
																
																Shortlisting: Candidates equal to 8 times the number of vacancies will be selected for the CBAT.
																
																
																Qualifying Marks: Candidates must secure a minimum T-Score of 42 in each of the test batteries to qualify. This applies to all candidates, regardless of community or category.
																
																
																Exam Type: This test contains questions and answer options only in English and Hindi.
																
																
																Negative Marking: There will be no negative marking in the CBAT.
																
																
																Merit List: The merit list will be drawn based on the candidates' performance in both the CBT (70% weightage) and the CBAT (30% weightage).
																
															

															Document Verification (DV)

															
																
																Candidates will be called for document verification based on the merit list prepared using a 70% weightage for marks obtained in CBT and a 30% weightage for marks obtained in CBAT.
																
																
																In case of a tie in marks, the merit position will be determined by age (the older person is placed higher) and then by the alphabetical order of the name.
																
															

															Minimum Qualifying Marks

															The minimum percentage of qualifying marks for the CBT is as follows:

															
																
																UR (Unreserved) & EWS (Economically Weaker Section): 40%
																
																
																OBC (Non-creamy layer): 30%
																
																
																SC (Scheduled Caste): 30%
																
																
																ST (Scheduled Tribe): 25%
																
															

															Note: The qualifying percentages for PwBD (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities) candidates are relaxed by 2 marks in case of a shortage of qualified candidates.

															RRB Section Controller CEN No. 04/2025: Exam Pattern/ Syllabus

															Computer Based Test (CBT)

															
																
																Total Duration: 120 minutes.
																
																
																Total Questions: 100 objective-type questions with multiple choices.
																
																
																Negative Marking: There will be negative marking, with a penalty of 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
																Normalization: The CBT will be held in multiple shifts, and a normalized score will be used for shortlisting candidates for the CBAT.
																
															

															CBT Syllabus

															The syllabus for the CBT is divided into three sections:

															
																
																Analytical and Mathematical Capability:

																
																	
																	Mathematics: Includes topics like Averages, Percentages, Profit, Loss & Discounts, Time, Speed, Distance, Power & Work, Algebra, Linear Equations, Arithmetic Progression, LCM, HCF, Geometry, Area & Volumes, Probability & Statistics (both basic level).
																	
																	
																	Data Analysis & Interpretation: Includes Multi-source Data Analysis, Examination, analysis and Inference drawing from text, tabular data and data represented graphically (charts, graphs, scatter plot, pie chart, statistical curve distribution, Venn Diagrams), Data Sufficiency, and Data Arrangement.
																	
																
																
																
																Logical Capability:

																
																	
																	Logical Reasoning: Includes Binary Logic, Syllogism, Clocks & Calendars, Assumptions, Blood Relations, Family Tree, and Solving logic-based puzzles.
																	
																	
																	Reading Comprehension: Passages would be given from subjects like History, Society, Literature, Science, Environment, Abstract, Mythology, Technology and Culture. Candidates will need to understand the main idea, supporting idea, application, logical structure, and style of the passage to answer questions.
																	
																
																
																
																Mental Reasoning:

																
																	
																	Analogy: Identifying the relationship between two terms and applying it to another pair.
																	
																	
																	Series Completion: Identifying the pattern in a sequence of numbers and predicting the next term.
																	
																	
																	Solving Coding-Decoding type questions, Solving Ranking and Arrangements based problems.
																	
																
																
															

															
															Section-Wise Question Distribution (Indicative)

															
																
																Analytical and Mathematical Capability: 60 questions
																
																
																Logical Capability: 20 questions
																
																
																Mental Reasoning: 20 questions
																
																
																Total: 100 questions
																
															
															

															Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

															
																
																Shortlisting: Candidates equal to 8 times the number of vacancies will be selected for the CBAT.
																
																
																Qualifying Marks: Candidates must secure a minimum T-Score of 42 in each of the test batteries to qualify. This applies to all candidates, regardless of community or category.
																
																
																Exam Type: This test contains questions and answer options only in English and Hindi.
																
																
																Negative Marking: There will be no negative marking in the CBAT.
																
																
																Merit List: The merit list will be drawn based on the candidates' performance in both the CBT (70% weightage) and the CBAT (30% weightage).
																
															

															Document Verification (DV)

															
																
																Candidates will be called for document verification based on the merit list prepared using a 70% weightage for marks obtained in CBT and a 30% weightage for marks obtained in CBAT.
																
																
																In case of a tie in marks, the merit position will be determined by age (the older person is placed higher) and then by the alphabetical order of the name.
																
															

															Minimum Qualifying Marks

															The minimum percentage of qualifying marks for the CBT is as follows:

															
																
																UR (Unreserved) & EWS (Economically Weaker Section): 40%
																
																
																OBC (Non-creamy layer): 30%
																
																
																SC (Scheduled Caste): 30%
																
																
																ST (Scheduled Tribe): 25%
																
															

															Note: The qualifying percentages for PwBD (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities) candidates are relaxed by 2 marks in case of a shortage of qualified candidates.

															UP Assistant Teacher 2026 Selection Process & Written Exam Pattern

															
																
																Selection Scheme:

																
																	
																	Selection for Assistant Teacher (Urban) and Assistant Teacher Attached Primary (Aided Non-Govt. School) posts will be based on a merit list prepared from a 360-Mark Written Examination.
																	
																
																
																
																Written Exam Highlights:

																
																	
																	Exam Mode / Question Type: Objective-Type Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) with 4 options each.
																	
																	
																	Total Questions: 120 Questions.
																	
																	
																	Total Marks: 360 Marks.
																	
																	
																	Exam Duration: 2 Hours (120 Minutes).
																	
																	
																	Marking Scheme: +3 Marks for each correct answer.
																	
																	
																	Negative Marking: 1 Mark deducted for every wrong or multiple-choice answer.
																	
																	
																	Medium of Exam: Bilingual (English & Hindi).
																	
																	
																	OMR Marking: Candidates must darken the correct circle on the OMR sheet using a black ballpoint pen.
																	
																
																
																
																Tie-Breaking Rules (In Case of Equal Merit):

																
																	
																	First Preference: Higher Graduation Percentage.
																	
																	
																	Second Preference: Higher Teacher Training Qualification Percentage.
																	
																	
																	Third Preference: Older candidate in age.
																	
																
																
																
																Result Declaration:

																
																	
																	The written exam cut-off marks and individual candidate scores will be displayed on the official website after the completion of the recruitment process.
																	
																
																
															
															
														
														
															
															Pay Scale & Mode of Selection

															
																Pay Scale: -Rs. 35,400 – 1,12,400 Pay Level 6, Grade Pay Rs. 4,200/-  
																Selection Process: Selection on the Basis of Written Exam & Merit List.

															UP Assistant Teacher 2026 Selection Process & Written Exam Pattern

															
																
																Selection Scheme:

																
																	
																	Selection for Assistant Teacher (Urban) and Assistant Teacher Attached Primary (Aided Non-Govt. School) posts will be based on a merit list prepared from a 360-Mark Written Examination.
																	
																
																
																
																Written Exam Highlights:

																
																	
																	Exam Mode / Question Type: Objective-Type Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) with 4 options each.
																	
																	
																	Total Questions: 120 Questions.
																	
																	
																	Total Marks: 360 Marks.
																	
																	
																	Exam Duration: 2 Hours (120 Minutes).
																	
																	
																	Marking Scheme: +3 Marks for each correct answer.
																	
																	
																	Negative Marking: 1 Mark deducted for every wrong or multiple-choice answer.
																	
																	
																	Medium of Exam: Bilingual (English & Hindi).
																	
																	
																	OMR Marking: Candidates must darken the correct circle on the OMR sheet using a black ballpoint pen.
																	
																
																
																
																Tie-Breaking Rules (In Case of Equal Merit):

																
																	
																	First Preference: Higher Graduation Percentage.
																	
																	
																	Second Preference: Higher Teacher Training Qualification Percentage.
																	
																	
																	Third Preference: Older candidate in age.
																	
																
																
																
																Result Declaration:

																
																	
																	The written exam cut-off marks and individual candidate scores will be displayed on the official website after the completion of the recruitment process.
																	
																
																
															
															
														
														
															
															Pay Scale & Mode of Selection

															
																Pay Scale: -Rs. 35,400 – 1,12,400 Pay Level 6, Grade Pay Rs. 4,200/-  
																Selection Process: Selection on the Basis of Written Exam & Merit List.

																		UPESSC PGT 2026 Selection Process & Written Exam Pattern

																		
																			
																			Total Marks & Selection Scheme:

																			
																				
																				Selection for Post Graduate Teacher (PGT / Lecturer) in Aided Non-Government Schools (Boys / Girls) will be based on a merit list out of 400 Total Marks (360 Marks for Written Exam + 40 Marks for Interview).
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Written Exam Overview:

																			
																				
																				Question Paper Distribution: Out of 120 total questions, 30 questions will be based on General Knowledge (GK) and 90 questions will be based on the Related Subject.
																				
																				
																				Total Marks: 360 Marks.
																				
																				
																				Duration: 2 Hours (120 Minutes).
																				
																				
																				Question Type: Objective Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) with 4 options each.
																				
																				
																				Marking Scheme: +3 Marks for every correct answer.
																				
																				
																				Negative Marking: 1 Mark deducted for every wrong or multiple-choice answer.
																				
																				
																				OMR Instructions: Answers must be marked on the OMR sheet using a black ballpoint pen.
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Interview Round:

																			
																				
																				Total Interview Marks: 40 Marks.
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Tie-Breaking Criteria (In Case of Equal Overall Marks):

																			
																				
																				Higher marks obtained in the Written Examination.
																				
																				
																				Higher marks obtained in the Interview.
																				
																				
																				Higher percentage in Post Graduation (Master's Degree).
																				
																				
																				Higher percentage in Teacher Training Qualification (B.Ed.).
																				
																				
																				Older candidate in age.
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Result Declaration:

																			
																				
																				Final cut-off marks and candidate scores will be updated on the official website after the completion of the recruitment process.
																				
																			
																			
																		
																		
																	
																	
																		
																		Pay Scale & Mode of Selection

																		
																			Pay Scale: -Rs. 47,600 – 1,51,100 Pay Level 8
																			Selection Process: Selection on the Basis of Written Exam, Interview & Merit List.

																		UPESSC PGT 2026 Selection Process & Written Exam Pattern

																		
																			
																			Total Marks & Selection Scheme:

																			
																				
																				Selection for Post Graduate Teacher (PGT / Lecturer) in Aided Non-Government Schools (Boys / Girls) will be based on a merit list out of 400 Total Marks (360 Marks for Written Exam + 40 Marks for Interview).
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Written Exam Overview:

																			
																				
																				Question Paper Distribution: Out of 120 total questions, 30 questions will be based on General Knowledge (GK) and 90 questions will be based on the Related Subject.
																				
																				
																				Total Marks: 360 Marks.
																				
																				
																				Duration: 2 Hours (120 Minutes).
																				
																				
																				Question Type: Objective Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) with 4 options each.
																				
																				
																				Marking Scheme: +3 Marks for every correct answer.
																				
																				
																				Negative Marking: 1 Mark deducted for every wrong or multiple-choice answer.
																				
																				
																				OMR Instructions: Answers must be marked on the OMR sheet using a black ballpoint pen.
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Interview Round:

																			
																				
																				Total Interview Marks: 40 Marks.
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Tie-Breaking Criteria (In Case of Equal Overall Marks):

																			
																				
																				Higher marks obtained in the Written Examination.
																				
																				
																				Higher marks obtained in the Interview.
																				
																				
																				Higher percentage in Post Graduation (Master's Degree).
																				
																				
																				Higher percentage in Teacher Training Qualification (B.Ed.).
																				
																				
																				Older candidate in age.
																				
																			
																			
																			
																			Result Declaration:

																			
																				
																				Final cut-off marks and candidate scores will be updated on the official website after the completion of the recruitment process.
																				
																			
																			
																		
																		
																	
																	
																		
																		Pay Scale & Mode of Selection

																		
																			Pay Scale: -Rs. 47,600 – 1,51,100 Pay Level 8
																			Selection Process: Selection on the Basis of Written Exam, Interview & Merit List.
